newsitem.title: CHILE: Pinochet denies pressure over Bolivia border.
newsitem.headline: Pinochet denies pressure over Bolivia border.

text.p: Former dictator General Augusto Pinochet, who still serves as army chief, denied that he pressured the Chilean government to not resolve a long border dispute with Bolivia, said newspaper El Mercurio on Saturday.
Bolivian Foreign Minister Antonio Aranibar sparked a diplomatic spat last week when he accused Pinochet of being an obstacle to land-locked Bolivia's efforts to regain access to the Pacific Ocean.
"What has been attributed to me is false," Pinochet told reporters in the southern Lake District where he was on holiday.
Chile made a verbal protest to Bolivia last week over Aranibar's remarks, which Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza described as "mistaken" and "absurd".
Pinochet said his government offered Bolivia a land exchange in the mid 1970s that would have given it access to the sea, but the discussions floundered without agreement.

Bolivia has long tried to persuade Chile to return part of the large stretch of the desolate Atacama Desert that it won in the 1879 War of the Pacific. The border was fixed by a treaty in 1904 but President Eduardo Frei's government has ruled out returning land to Bolivia, although it has offered to improve road and rail links.
The frontier dispute dominates relations between the two countries, which have not had formal diplomatic ties for nearly 20 years.
